tasks.title: Print the welcome
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `Notice.java`, print this line:

```
Welcome to Lanternquay Ferries
```

Check compiles and runs your Task 1 lines, and looks for a line that matches this one exactly, capital letters and spaces included.
nextSteps: Run `java Notice.java` once and read what it prints today.
Look at the line that prints the good morning: it is your model.
Write a new line under `// Task 1` that prints the welcome.
Run the program again and compare the output with the task.
hints: The program already prints one line. Read how that line is written, down to the semicolon at its end.
Text sits inside double quotes, the quotes sit inside the round brackets, and the statement ends with a semicolon.
The line has the shape `System.out.println("...");`, with the welcome where the dots are.

tasks.title: Print the crossing times
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, print the two lines of the crossing times, in this order:

```
Boats cross every half hour
Last boat back at half past seven
```

Check compiles and runs your Task 2 lines and looks for both lines, the second right after the first.
nextSteps: Find `// Task 2` and read the two lines in the comment.
Print the first line with its own `System.out.println`.
Print the second line on the line below it.
Run the program and read the output from top to bottom.
hints: One `System.out.println` prints one line. How many lines are there?
Java runs the lines inside main from top to bottom, so the order you write them in is the order they print in.
Two `System.out.println("...");` lines, one under the other, each with one of the times in double quotes.

tasks.title: Print the hours on one line
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, two lines print the hut's hours on two lines. Change how the first one prints, so both parts come out on one line, and the line ends after them:

```
Hut open from 6:30 to 20:00
```

Keep both lines. Check compiles and runs your Task 3 lines, looks for that one line, and reads your lines to see that there are still two and that the first prints in the other way the lesson shows.
nextSteps: Run the program and find the hours in the output: they are on two lines.
Read the part of the lesson about the two ways to print.
Change the first of the two lines, not its text.
Run the program again: the hours should be on one line.
hints: Both lines use the same way of printing. The lesson shows two.
`println` ends the line after it prints. The other way leaves the line open, so the next print carries on right after it.
Change the first line to `System.out.print("Hut open from 6:30 ");` and leave the second as it is.

tasks.title: Switch off the old notice
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4` there is a line that prints a notice the hut no longer runs. Turn it into a comment, so it stays in the file but no longer runs.

Check compiles and runs your Task 4 lines to see that the notice is not printed, then reads them to see that the line is still there as a comment.
nextSteps: Run the program and find the old notice in the output.
Find the line under `// Task 4` that prints it.
Turn that one line into a comment. Do not delete it.
Run the program again: the notice should be gone from the output.
hints: The lesson shows a way to keep a line in the file while Java skips it.
Every comment in this file starts the same way. Look at the start of the lines that do not print anything.
Put `//` at the very start of the notice's line.
